name: Stablecoin market-cap expansion regime + RSI dip — buy dips with dry powder present (spot long)
rationale: MECHANISM (why the stablecoin float leads the dip-buy): total stablecoin market cap is crypto's standing dry powder — a large float is fiat parked and ready to deploy on weakness. In a high-float regime, dips get absorbed by sidelined capital rotating in, so an RSI dip is a buying opportunity rather than the start of an exodus. The float is a slow, structural liquidity backdrop that conditions how dips resolve. We require stablecoin_mcap above a fitted floor (ample powder) AND an RSI dip (timing); exit on RSI reverting up. This uses the LEVEL (standing powder) where the sister spec uses the FLOW (fresh minting). DISCONFIRMER 1: if a plain RSI-dip buy without the mcap gate matches the deflated Sharpe, the float adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 2 (CRITICAL — non-stationarity): stablecoin mcap grew near-monotonically (~$5B→$160B), so a fitted absolute floor is almost certainly always-true and the 'regime' is fake; the Gate's deflated Sharpe MUST kill it unless the level genuinely partitions dip outcomes. Data knowable T+1. tier1, low-confidence until OOS.
catalyst: stablecoin_mcap is above a fitted floor (large stablecoin float = ample dry powder) while RSI has dipped.
